title: DeviceInfo
description: LSP/1 DeviceInfo: body of GET /info and POST /register, and the `sender` member of a SessionRequest. Mirrors packages/libreshare_core/lib/src/model/device.dart. `required` lists only the members a receiver cannot default; senders SHOULD emit every member. Unknown members MUST be ignored. `fingerprint` is the uppercase hex SHA-256 of the DER certificate; it is the empty string in the plaintext profile (Increments 1 and 2, and the loopback/test profile afterwards) and always 64 characters in the LSP/1.1 secure profile (Increment 3), where `v` is `1.1`.

v.description: Protocol version major.minor. Default `1.0` (plaintext profile). A device in the LSP/1.1 secure profile reports `1.1` (kProtocolVersionSecure). The major selects the API path (/api/v<major>); a peer with any 1.x is accepted by both profiles.

deviceId.description: Stable device identifier (UUID v4 in production).

alias.description: Human-readable device name shown to the peer.

platform.description: Free-form platform tag, e.g. windows, linux, android, macos, ios. Default `unknown`.

deviceType.description: Form factor, e.g. desktop, mobile. Default `desktop`.

fingerprint.description: Uppercase hex SHA-256 of the DER-encoded self-signed certificate (64 chars). Empty string in the plaintext profile (no certificate); non-empty in the secure profile, where it MUST equal the hash of the certificate presented in the TLS handshake. Default empty.

port.description: TCP port of the HTTP(S) API. Default 53318. 0 means this instance runs no API listener (a send-only client such as `ls send`); an announcement always carries a real port (see discovery-announce).

addrs.description: Connection candidates for this device. Default empty.

if.description: Interface class: wifi, ethernet or unknown (default). Other values MUST be treated as unknown.

caps.description: Capability tokens. Defined: resume, tunnel (Increment 5), sas (the device serves POST /sessions/{sid}/sas, LSP/1.1 [I3]), pair (the device serves POST /pair, LSP/1.1 [I3]). A sender checks `sas`/`pair` before using the route; a LSP/1.0 peer answers 404. Unknown tokens are ignored.
